newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police catch, and release, wanted neo-Nazi.
newsitem.headline: German police catch, and release, wanted neo-Nazi.

text.p: German police on Friday finally caught a leading neo-Nazi who has been wanted for years on suspicion of spreading racist propaganda -- then freed him when a doctor ruled he was too ill to be taken into custody.

Prosecutors in the far northern town of Flensburg said they had detained Thies Christophersen, a Nazi apologist well into his 70s who moved to Denmark in 1986 and for years published Nazi pamphlets from just across the German border.
Christophersen is also the author of a book, well known among neo-Nazis, called "The Auschwitz Lie" in which he claims the Nazi massacre of six million Jews in the Holocaust is a myth.
Germany has been seeking him to answer charges of inciting racial hatred, but failed to get him extradited from Denmark.
A spokesman for Flensburg prosecutors said Christophersen, who has a house not far from the place where he was arrested near Kiel, was in "desolate health" when he was detained.
